etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English tubbe, tobbe, from Middle Dutch tubbe or Middle Low German tubbe, tobbe, further etymology unknown. Considered to be unrelated to tube.

definitions.definition: A flat-bottomed vessel, of width similar to or greater than its height, used for storing or packing things, or for washing things in.
The contents or capacity of such a vessel.

quote.citation: 1920, Theodore Sharpe, My Place in the Shade: And Various Verse, page 27:
quote.text: Teach me to love my morning tub, / In waters cold to splash and rub; / O, grant my Turkish towel may flood / Its virtues through my soul and blood.

quote.citation: 2019 March 13, Drachinifel, 24:52 from the start, in The Russian 2nd Pacific Squadron - Voyage of the Damned‎[1], archived from the original on 15 October 2022:
quote.text: But, with any ships in the Baltic Fleet that were worth sending - and some that probably weren't worth sending anyway - having already been dispatched, this gave him the perfect excuse to start rounding up old, obsolete vessels which had been rejected in the first place as being old tubs and designated by some of the less-kind officers as the "Sink-by-Themselves Squadron".

definitions.definition: (humorous or derogatory) Any structure shaped like a tub, such as a certain old form of pulpit, a short broad boat, etc.

quote.citation: 1692–1717, Robert South, Twelve Sermons Preached upon Several Occasions, volume (please specify |volume=I to VI), London:
quote.text: All being took up and busied, some in pulpits and some in tubs, in the grand work of preaching and holding forth.

definitions.definition: Any of various historically designated quantities of goods to be sold by the tub (butter, oysters, etc).
(mining) A box or bucket in which coal or ore is sent up a shaft.
(obsolete) A sweating in a tub; a tub fast.

quote.citation: c. 1605–1608, William Shakespeare, “The Life of Tymon of Athens”, in Mr. William Shakespeares Comedies, Histories, & Tragedies […] (First Folio), London:  […]  Isaac Iaggard, and Ed[ward] Blount, published 1623, →OCLC, [Act IV, scene iii]:
quote.text: tubs and baths; bring down rose-cheeked youth To the tub-fast and the diet

quote.citation: 2003, Trey Ellis, Platitudes: & the New Black Aesthetic, page 139:
quote.text: Donald tells him to be more realistic. Take those two girls over there, for example. One's a zitface and the other's a tub, so they'd be perfect for them.

definitions.definition: (automotive) The bare body shell of an automobile (minus the doors, hood, trunk lid, fenders, etc.) which is lowered onto the chassis at the time of assembly, or in the case of modern unibody designed vehicles, is itself a monocoque around which the rest of the vehicle is built.

quote.citation: 2017 February 10, Máté Petrány, McLaren Will Start Building its Own Carbon Fiber Tubs‎[2], archived from the original on 31 August 2023:
quote.text: Every street or race car McLaren has built since 1981 uses a carbon fiber tub. Now, McLaren will make them in-house.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To plant, set, or store in a tub.
(transitive, intransitive) To bathe in a tub.

quote.citation: February 1, 1873, Meredith Townsend and Richard Holt Hutton (editors), "Change of Air and Scene", in The Spectator
